basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 2.' and it opens 'Vers. 2. Castra Dei sunt haec. Id est angelica agmina. Et bene pergenti Jacob ad fratrem'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 2. Castra Dei sunt haec. Id est angelica agmina. Et bene pergenti Jacob ad fratrem obvii fuerunt angeli Dei, ut videlicet per hoc confortaretur et non metueret fratrem securus de angelico auxilio.
